summary: Palette, density and per-pixel independence match well, but the port has no twinkle envelope at all: it re-randomizes every pixel roughly 20 times a second where the original fades each pixel smoothly up and down over ~1.9 s, so the original reads as gentle twinkling and the port as harsh orange/violet static.
observations: Neither side exposes any settable control (probe: 'no settable controls' on orig and port); no compile or runtime errors on either side in any run; both sides wantsSensors=false.

Rig is a 60 px strip. Both sides are alive and steady across the whole 240 s survey and at --skip 60: brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 0, no modes, regimes, drift or death on either side. The survey texture is uniform end-to-end, so there is only one regime to compare.

Temporal envelope is the divergence. Per-pixel brightness traces from --dump at 0.05 s spacing (label dump-long, 200 frames over 10 s at 20 fps): the original ramps each pixel smoothly on and off, e.g. px10 runs 0,45,98,167,229,254,227,160,86,34,0 across ~0.55 s of rise and fall, then stays dark ~2 s before re-igniting. The port's px10 over the same 11 frames is 0, orange 226, 0, violet 172/0/246, 0, violet 165/0/238, orange 142/34/0, 0, 0, ... -- it jumps between black and a fresh random colour every frame with no intermediate values.

Quantified: median lit-run per pixel is 37 frames = 1.85 s on the original and 1 frame = 0.05 s on the port (20 fps, 60 px, 10 s window); median dark gap 44 frames = 2.20 s on the original. Ignition rate per pixel is 0.18/s original vs 6.19/s port -- the port twinkles ~34x too often.

Per-pixel brightness autocorrelation (raw series, lag scan): original decays smoothly 1.00, 0.99, 0.97, 0.95, 0.92, ... crossing half at lag 13 frames = 0.65 s. Port is 1.00 then -0.31 at lag 1 and noise thereafter -- anti-correlated at one frame, i.e. white noise, no envelope whatsoever.
Whole-window motion stat matches that: baseline (6 s, 20 fps) orig motion avg 2 / motionLit 4.7, port motion avg 53 / motionLit 68.9 -- ~25x. Same ratio at --skip 60 and across all seeds.

Both sides are TIME-based, not frame-coupled -- this is not an fps-coupling bug. Original motion is 4 / 2 / 1 at 10 / 20 / 40 fps (halving as fps doubles = constant change per second) and its median lit-run is 1.85 s at 20 fps and 1.70 s at 40 fps. The port's median lit-run is 1 frame at 20 fps and 2 frames at 40 fps -- both 0.050 s. The port simply re-randomizes on a ~20 Hz clock instead of fading.

Colour family is close on both sides: two fully-saturated lobes, orange and violet, no other hues, mean saturation 1.000 on both. Fine hue histogram (lit pixels, value>20, dump-long window) -- orig orange 5-25 deg peaking at 10 deg, violet 250-290 deg peaking at 265 deg; port orange 5-30 deg peaking at 10 deg, violet 250-300 deg with mass spread out to 300 deg. The port's violet lobe is noticeably wider and pushed further toward magenta.

Density matches: lit fraction 0.487 orig vs 0.452 port; mean value of lit pixels 130 orig vs 150 port (the port is brighter per lit pixel because it never renders the dim rising/falling part of a fade).

Spatial character matches: both are stationary per-pixel twinkles, not travelling features. Circular cross-correlation of frames 0.5/1/2 s apart on the original best-aligns at shift 0, +2, -1 px (no consistent drift); spatial autocorrelation at lags 1-7 is ~0 on both sides, so neighbouring pixels twinkle independently on both. The diagonal streaks visible in the 5 fps survey waterfall are sampling aliasing, not real motion.

Frame-to-frame whole-strip stability differs as a consequence: original meanBrightness stays in 26-34 over the late window, the port swings 15-49, because the port flips its entire strip at once every ~0.05 s.

Not a seed fluke: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give identical stats on both sides (orig motion 2 / port motion 53 in every case) and visually identical character. That the seeds render identically is a fact about the seeds here, not evidence about the pattern; the orig/port divergence is unchanged at all three.
feedback: The port is missing the fade envelope entirely -- this is the one thing to fix. Each pixel must ramp its brightness smoothly from 0 up to full and back down over roughly 1.9 s (measured median lit-run 37 frames at 20 fps), then stay dark for roughly 2.2 s before the next twinkle. The port currently holds each pixel's value for only ~0.05 s and picks a new random colour and brightness on the next update.

Target ignition rate is about 0.18 new twinkles per pixel per second (a given pixel lights up roughly every 5.5 s). The port is at 6.19/s -- about 34x too fast. Slowing the update clock alone is not enough; the intermediate brightness values must be interpolated, not stepped.

A pixel's HUE must stay fixed for the whole life of its twinkle -- the original holds one colour while only brightness moves (px10 keeps R:G at ~4.6:1 through its entire 98 -> 254 ramp). The port re-rolls the hue on every update, so a single pixel flips orange/violet/orange within a tenth of a second.

Keep what already works: the two-lobe orange+violet fully-saturated palette, ~46% lit density, and independent per-pixel (non-travelling, spatially uncorrelated) twinkles are all correct and should not be changed.

Minor colour nitpick once the envelope is fixed: the port's violet lobe is wider than the original's. Original violet sits in 250-290 deg peaking at 265 deg; port spreads to 300 deg with visible magenta. Original orange sits in 5-25 deg; port reaches 30 deg. Tighten both hue ranges slightly.
